parts.name: Renal Cortex
parts.description: The outer reddish-brown parenchymal zone extending from the fibrous renal capsule to the base of the medullary pyramids, dipping inward between pyramids as the Renal Columns of Bertin. Contains all 1-1.2 million glomeruli and convoluted tubules.
parts.function: Executes initial high-pressure plasma ultrafiltration across the glomerular filtration barrier (~180 L/day GFR), reabsorbing 65-70% of filtered water, sodium, potassium, and 100% of filtered glucose and amino acids in proximal convoluted tubules.
connections: Enclosed externally by Perirenal Fat Capsule and Renal Fascia of Gerota
Continuous internally with medullary ray projections and Columns of Bertin
Supplied by Interlobular Arteries giving rise to Afferent Arterioles
Houses the Juxtaglomerular Apparatus (macula densa + JG cells) regulating renin release
parts.clinicalNote: Susceptible to immune complex deposition (Glomerulonephritis) and acute tubular necrosis (ATN) during ischemic shock or nephrotoxic drug exposure (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, IV contrast). Loss of cortical thickness (<1 cm) on ultrasound indicates chronic kidney disease (CKD).
keyFeatures: Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR) benchmark: 90 - 120 mL/min/1.73 m2
Produces Erythropoietin (EPO) in response to peritubular capillary hypoxia
1-alpha-hydroxylase site activating 25-OH Vitamin D into active Calcitriol
Houses 85% Cortical Nephrons with short loops of Henle
parts.histology: Bowman capsules enclosing fenestrated capillary loops, podocyte pedicels with slit diaphragms (filtration barrier), and proximal tubule cuboidal epithelium with dense microvillar brush border.

parts.name: Renal Pelvis & Calyces
parts.description: The funnel-shaped proximal dilated expansion of the ureter residing within the renal sinus at the medial hilum, formed by the convergence of 2-3 major calyces, which in turn receive urine from 7-14 minor calyces capping the renal papillae.
parts.function: Collects processed urine excreted from the papillary ducts of Bellini, utilizing intrinsic pacemaking smooth muscle cells to generate peristaltic contractions that pump urine towards the ureter and urinary bladder.
connections: Receives urine discharge from Minor Calyces enveloping Renal Papillae
Major Calyces unite at the Renal Hilum to form the single Renal Pelvis
Tapers posteroinferiorly at the Ureteropelvic Junction (UPJ) to become the Ureter
Lies posterior to the Renal Vein and Renal Artery within the hilar vascular pedicle
parts.clinicalNote: Common site for Staghorn calculi (struvite stones secondary to Proteus mirabilis UTI) and Ureteropelvic Junction (UPJ) obstruction leading to hydronephrosis, parenchymal thinning, and renal colic with costovertebral angle (CVA) tenderness (Murphy's punch test).
keyFeatures: Lined with impermeant transitional urothelium preventing solute back-diffusion
Hydronephrosis grading detects pelvic dilation on ultrasound
parts.histology: Urothelium (transitional epithelium) featuring umbrella cells with apical asymmetric unit membrane plaques, overlying a lamina propria and double helical smooth muscle layers.

parts.name: Ureter
parts.description: A paired muscular retroperitoneal tubular conduit (25-30 cm in length, 3-4 mm caliber) descending vertically along the anterior surface of the Psoas major muscle from the renal pelvis down across the pelvic brim into the posterior base of the bladder.
parts.function: Propels urine continuously from the renal pelvis into the urinary bladder via rhythmic, myogenic unidirectional peristaltic waves independent of gravity.
connections: Crosses pelvic brim anterior to the bifurcation of Common Iliac Artery
Courses inferomedially in pelvis, pierced obliquely in bladder wall (Ureterovesical Junction / UVJ)
Crossed anteriorly by gonadal vessels ('water under the bridge')
parts.clinicalNote: Three classic physiological constriction sites where kidney stones lodge: (1) UPJ, (2) Pelvic brim iliac crossing, and (3) UVJ (most common). Causes excruciating colicky flank pain radiating to groin/labia/scrotum with gross or microscopic hematuria.
keyFeatures: Oblique intramural tunnel in bladder acts as a physiological anti-reflux flap valve
Failure of flap mechanism causes Vesicoureteral Reflux (VUR) and recurrent pyelonephritis
Receives multi-segmental arterial supply from renal, gonadal, and vesical branches
parts.histology: Transitional epithelium (urothelium) supported by inner longitudinal and outer circular smooth muscle layers (reversed relative to GI tract), surrounded by adventitia.

quizBank.prompt: What percentage of daily glomerular filtrate is reabsorbed back into circulation?
quizBank.rationale: Of the 180 liters of daily filtrate, over 99% is reabsorbed, excreting approximately 1 to 2 liters as urine.
